title: Epoch
body: One complete pass through the entire training dataset. During each epoch, the model sees and learns from every training example exactly once before weights are updated.

title: Gradient Descent
body: An optimization algorithm used to minimize a loss function by iteratively moving in the direction of steepest descent. Parameters are updated in the negative direction of the gradient.

title: Backpropagation
body: An algorithm for calculating gradients of the loss function with respect to the weights in a neural network. Efficiently computes gradients by recursively applying the chain rule through network layers.

title: Overfitting
body: A condition in machine learning where a model learns the training data too well, including its noise and peculiarities, resulting in poor generalization to unseen data. The model memorizes rather than learns patterns.

title: Regularization
body: A technique used to prevent overfitting by adding a penalty term to the loss function. Common methods include L1 (Lasso), L2 (Ridge) regularization, and dropout, which constrain model complexity.

title: Transformer
body: A deep learning architecture based on self-attention mechanisms that allows models to weigh different parts of input data differently. Powers modern LLMs like GPT and BERT.

title: Accuracy
body: A classification metric that measures the proportion of correct predictions (both true positives and true negatives) to the total number of predictions. Defined as (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN).

title: F1 Score
body: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a single metric that balances both false positives and false negatives. Useful when class distribution is imbalanced. Defined as 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall).
